jobs.title: Associate Director, Strategy & Operations – US Market Access & Reimbursement
jobs.description:
About This Role
The Associate Director of Strategy and Operations plays a critical role in ensuring the US Market Access & Reimbursement (MA&R) organization is positioned to deliver on its strategy and business priorities by driving alignment, preparedness, and operational discipline. This role will partner closely with cross-functional leaders across Commercial, Franchises, Medical, and Finance, to support strategic planning, meeting preparation, and operating rhythm execution.
This position is designed to be the strategic operator and integrator for the MA&R team, driving day-to-day coordination, synthesizing cross-functional inputs, preparing high-quality executive materials, and ensuring timely execution of deliverables. This is a high-visibility role requiring strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills with the ability to work in a fast-moving, highly matrixed environment.
This role reports to the Senior Director of Strategy and Operations.

What You’ll Do
- Strategic & Operating Rhythm Support - Partner with the Head of Strategy & Ops to run the MA&R operating model, including standing leadership forums and performance/execution updates
- Lead meeting preparation: develop agendas, synthesize updates, draft executive-ready pre-reads, and coordinate follow-ups and action tracking
- Maintain and manage performance related trackers and milestone dashboards
- Ensure clear alignment and timely execution across cross functional groups.

- Budget, Resourcing & Operational Tracking - Support the operational budget process, and tracking and coordination of the Market Access functional budget, in partnership with finance, SD of Strat & Ops, and LT
- Track deliverables, performance indicators, and operational progress needed for executive reviews

- Operational Excellence & Execution - Drive continuous improvement of business processes to enable execution across MA&R
- Identify and remove barriers to execution across access, pricing, reimbursement, and payer engagement strategies
- Lead or support cross-functional initiatives that enable payer readiness and sustained access performance

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree required, MBA or advanced degree preferred
- 7+ years of experience in consulting, pharmaceutical operations, market access, or related biopharma roles
- Proven business acumen (e.g., MBA, business leadership experience, or equivalent)
- Strong planning, project management, and cross-functional coordination capabilities
- Exceptional written communication skills, with ability to produce boardroom-ready materials (decision-oriented pre-reads, executive summaries, and complex cross-functional syntheses)
- Negotiation and influence skills, with the ability to drive alignment among cross-functional stakeholders, manage competing priorities, and secure commitments without formal authority
- Ability to synthesize complex inputs into clear, actionable storylines
- Experience preparing materials for senior leadership forums
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills
- Strong accountability mindset with a track record of driving execution
- Proficiency with business tools (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Word)

Preferred Qualifications
- MBA or advanced degree
- Experience in Market Access & Reimbursement, including payer strategy, pricing, etc.
- Experience and deep understanding of healthcare ecosystems
- Experience supporting product launches or major access initiatives
- Change management experience in complex organizations

Job Level: Management
Additional Information

The base compensation range for this role is: -
Base salary offered is determined through an analytical approach utilizing a combination of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills & experience, job location, and internal equity.

Regular employees are eligible to receive both short term and long-term incentives, including cash bonus and equity incentive opportunities, designed to reward recent achievements and recognize your future potential based on individual, business unit and company performance.

In addition to compensation, Biogen offers a full and highly competitive range of benefits designed to support our employees’ and their families physical, financial, emotional, and social well-being ; including, but not limited to:
- Medical, Dental, Vision, & Life insurances

jobs.title: Director, Finance Transformation
jobs.description:
About This Role:

As the Director of Finance Transformation, you will be at the forefront of Biogen’s finance and IT modernization initiatives and the strategic owner of these workstreams within the FP&A organization. This newly created role is pivotal in bridging finance and technology, ensuring that enterprise-wide initiatives such as system enhancements, process automation, and AI-enabled analytics are designed and delivered to advance FP&A’s capabilities. You will define what FP&A needs from transformation efforts, influence cross-functional prioritization, and hold stakeholders accountable to finance outcomes. With deep FP&A experience and having lived through major systems implementations, you are energized by the broad scope and opportunity to make a lasting impact on FP&A operations. Your contributions will enhance FP&A's ability to service the business, fitting seamlessly into Biogen’s overall business structure.

What You’ll Do:
- Define and maintain a multi-year view of FP&A’s technology and process needs, focusing on enterprise data strategy, planning, and reporting architecture.
- Translate FP&A strategy into actionable requirements across key initiatives including system modernization and reporting evolution.
- Drive the AI roadmap for FP&A, identifying high-value use cases such as predictive forecasting and automated variance analysis.
- Represent FP&A in finance system design and modernization efforts, ensuring alignment with operational requirements.
- Partner with IT and data engineering on the enterprise finance data strategy, embedding FP&A’s reporting and analytics needs.
- Review systems deliverables to ensure they meet FP&A’s functional and operational requirements.
- Monitor finance workstream progress, proactively identifying risks and ensuring milestones are met.
- Engage thoughtfully with vendor proposals and project roadmaps, evaluating recommendations with technical fluency.
- Lead the development and integration of FP&A’s reporting and visualization capabilities into a scalable environment.
- Expand analytical capabilities, including tools for outlier detection and predictive forecasting.
- Communicate transformation priorities clearly to Senior Finance leaders and drive adoption within FP&A through training.

Who You Are:

You are a visionary leader who thrives in a dynamic environment, with a passion for transforming finance operations through innovation and strategic thinking. You possess a deep understanding of FP&A and have the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable finance strategies. Your collaborative nature and strong communication skills make you an effective bridge between finance and technology teams. You are committed to driving change and are motivated by the opportunity to make a significant impact on business performance.

Required Skills:
- 12+ years of experience in FP&A with expertise in financial planning, forecasting, and management reporting.
- Direct, hands-on experience in at least one full-cycle ERP or EPM implementation such as Oracle, Workday, SAP, or Anaplan.
- Familiarity with AI/ML applications in finance such as driver-based forecasting and anomaly detection.
- Ability to translate finance and technology requirements, write functional requirements, and review data models.
- Experience in a matrixed environment working with IT, business leaders, shared services, and external vendors.
- Proven track record of operating at a senior stakeholder level with credibility and influence.
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field.

Preferred Skills:
- Background in biopharma, life sciences, or healthcare.
- Familiarity with modern data infrastructure concepts such as data warehouses and BI tooling.
- MBA or CPA.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Program Management, Global Commercial Medical IT
jobs.description:
About This Role:
As the Associate Director of Program Management within the Global Commercial and Medical (GCM) IT organization, you will lead intricate, cross-functional programs and oversee portfolio financials, including governance, annual budgeting, and month-end close. You will drive critical projects and product launches supporting our Patient Services Organization in RTP, NC, ensuring they are delivered on time, within budget, and with minimal oversight. Your role is pivotal in collaborating with stakeholders to drive decisions and proactively manage and mitigate issues and risks, consolidate portfolio-level status reporting and track performance, ensuring the portfolio delivers high-quality outcomes. You will support the GCM Leadership Team with monthly portfolio reviews and manage ad hoc requests as needed. Reporting to the Director of Portfolio Management and Operations for Global Commercial and Medical IT, you will be a key player in driving the success and efficiency of our organizational projects.
What You’ll Do:
- Lead highly complex cross-functional projects and programs, including Patient Services initiatives, product launch programs and mergers & acquisitions.
- Consolidate project and program-level status reporting into a comprehensive portfolio view.
- Support month-end and portfolio reporting, focusing on financials and performance metrics.
- Drive large programs to ensure alignment on scope, schedule, resources, and budgets.
- Proactively manage key stakeholders, ensuring accountability and timely completion of deliverables.
- Clearly communicate financial status, schedule, risks, and changes to all stakeholders.
- Facilitate cross-team discussions for integrated project plans and communications.
- Identify and resolve issues to keep projects on track.
- Review financials for the GCM IT portfolio, ensuring accuracy and adherence to financial calendars.
- Identify efficiencies and areas of improvement for portfolio operations.

Who You Are:
You are a strategic thinker who thrives in managing complex and cross-functional programs. Your attention to detail and organizational skills ensure that projects are delivered with precision and high quality. You possess excellent communication skills that keep stakeholders informed and engaged, and you excel at managing financials and identifying areas for improvement. You work well under pressure, maintaining focus and delivering results with minimal supervision. Your ability to manage shifting priorities and timelines makes you an invaluable asset to our team.
Required Skills:
- A Master's degree in Information Technology, an MBA preferred or equivalent experience.
- 10+ years of experience as an IT professional managing projects, programs, and portfolios in the Pharma-Biotech industry.
- Significant program leadership experience in Patient Services and/or Patient Support Organizations.
- 5+ years of experience implementing complex, cross-functional projects within established software development life cycle methodologies.
- Experience managing projects through waterfall, agile, or SAFe delivery methodologies.
- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- Financial discipline and accountability for deliverables.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to manage shifting priorities and timelines effectively.

Preferred Skills:
- Experience managing product launches and/or mergers & acquisitions.
- Process-oriented mindset with the ability to identify efficiencies.
